items.title: Kimi pushed open weights into frontier territory
items.oneliner: Kimi K3.1 Pro brings 1M context and top coding scores, making open-weight models newly credible for serious production work.

items.title: Block unveiled a speech-only conversation model
items.oneliner: Block's speech-trained Dessa suggests voice agents may stop inheriting text-first biases and start sounding native to audio.

items.title: HTTP2Shell widened a critical Brotli attack
items.oneliner: A 9.2 CVSS Brotli flaw now hits multiple HTTP stacks, so disable decoding fast if your patch chain lags.

items.title: AI citations failed inside a published paper
items.oneliner: An AI-assisted Z-Library paper cited a nonexistent TorrentFreak story, which is exactly why automated research needs verification gates.

items.title: Apple reopened iPhone security research access
items.oneliner: Apple is again lending research iPhones, a practical signal that serious mobile security still depends on outside hackers.

items.title: Banking apps are slowly accepting GrapheneOS
items.oneliner: Around a dozen banking apps now allow GrapheneOS, showing mobile trust checks can loosen without collapsing fraud controls.

items.title: A kernel hack unlocked RTX 3000 throughput
items.oneliner: GPU-unlock reportedly doubles FP and BF16 issue rates on RTX 3000 cards, which could reshape low-budget local training economics.

items.title: Astral merged environment and type workflows
items.oneliner: Astral's uv plus ty integration turns Python setup and checking into one path, which is exactly what fragmented tooling needed.

items.title: Java gained a cleaner path to GPUs
items.oneliner: TornadoVM 7.3 moves Java GPU acceleration beyond JNI, making heterogeneous compute less painful for existing enterprise stacks.

items.title: Google's data center expansion hit environmental limits
items.oneliner: Finnish authorities halted parts of Google's data center build after 250,000 trees were cut, reminding AI infrastructure has physical costs.
